title: The City of the Great King
superscription: A song. A Psalm of the sons of Korah.

verses.text: Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, His holy mountain.
Beautiful in loftiness, the joy of all the earth, like the peaks of Zaphon is Mount Zion, the city of the great King.
God is in her citadels; He has shown Himself to be a fortress.
For behold, the kings assembled; they all advanced together.
They saw and were astounded; they fled in terror.
Trembling seized them there, anguish like a woman in labor.
With a wind from the east You wrecked the ships of Tarshish.
As we have heard, so we have seen in the city of the LORD of Hosts, in the city of our God: God will establish her forever. Selah
Within Your temple, O God, we contemplate Your loving devotion.
Your name, O God, like Your praise, reaches to the ends of the earth; Your right hand is full of righteousness.
Mount Zion is glad, the daughters of Judah rejoice, on account of Your judgments.
March around Zion, encircle her, count her towers,
consider her ramparts, tour her citadels, that you may tell the next generation.
For this God is our God forever and ever; He will be our guide even till death.

context.author: The title names the sons of Korah, a family of Levites descended from the Korah who rebelled against Moses (Numbers 16). His sons did not die with him (Numbers 26:11), and their descendants became gatekeepers and singers at the Temple (1 Chronicles 9:19; 2 Chronicles 20:19).
context.genre: Psalm: a song or prayer in Hebrew poetry
context.audience: Israel at worship in Jerusalem, and every reader who prays
context.setting: “Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, His holy mountain” (v.1). Zion is “beautiful in loftiness, the joy of all the earth, like the peaks of Zaphon… the city of the great King” (v.2). Kings gathered against it, saw, and fled in terror, as God wrecked “the ships of Tarshish” with an east wind (vv.4-7). “As we have heard, so we have seen” (v.8). In the Temple the worshipers think on His loving devotion (v.9). Then: “March around Zion, encircle her, count her towers, consider her ramparts… that you may tell the next generation. For this God is our God forever and ever; He will be our guide even till death” (vv.12-14).
context.custom: Zaphon (Mount Casius, Jebel Aqra in Syria) was the sacred mountain of the Canaanite gods; the psalm says Zion, a modest hill, is the true mountain of God. Ships of Tarshish were large sea-going vessels for long voyages (1 Kings 10:22). Pilgrims walked around the city walls, admiring them, before going home.
context.timelineImmediate: Psalm 49 teaches that riches cannot ransom a life from death.
context.timelineBible: Jesus told His hearers not to swear by Jerusalem, “for it is the city of the great King” (Matthew 5:35), quoting v.2. Hebrews says believers have come “to Mount Zion, to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem” (Hebrews 12:22).

translation.meaning: North; also Zaphon, the mountain of the gods in the north.
A distant port; “ships of Tarshish” are great ocean-going ships.
To lead, drive, guide, as a shepherd leads a flock.

gospelParallels.note: Jerusalem, the city of the great King.
The holy city, the new Jerusalem.

otBackground.note: The king’s fleet of ships of Tarshish.
The mountain of the LORD’s house.

overview.summary: Pilgrims praise Zion as the city of the great King, where enemy kings fled in terror, and walk around its towers to tell the next generation that this God is their guide forever.

archaeology.t: Mount Zaphon on the Syrian coast, worshiped as the home of Baal.
Part of Jerusalem’s 8th-century BC wall, uncovered in the Jewish Quarter.

overview.discussion: “That you may tell the next generation” (v.13). What have I seen of God that I need to pass on to someone younger?
overview.book: The book of Psalms · 150 psalms (1-125 in the app so far). Israel’s songs and prayers: praise, lament, thanks, trust and wisdom, many of them by David.
overview.author: The sons of Korah
